name: Periodic whole-day fasting

lead: Periodic whole-day fasting means going without food, usually water-only, for 24 hours or longer on a recurring or occasional basis. It is one of the forms of intermittent fasting, alongside time-restricted eating, alternate-day fasting and the 5:2 diet.

The appearance goal is leanness: a lower body-fat level shows up as a sharper jawline, less facial puffiness and a more defined physique. Trials of 24-hour fasting cycles mostly measure weight, body composition and metabolic markers, and report results broadly similar to ordinary calorie restriction.

paras: People typically pick one or more days per week or month, finish a meal, drink only water (some add unsweetened tea or coffee or electrolytes) for a day or longer, then return to normal meals. Some combine fasts with training days or with a calorie-controlled diet in the other days.

Reported effects include hunger, irritability, headaches and dizziness; longer fasts carry risks of electrolyte shifts and refeeding syndrome, and rapid weight loss can raise gallstone risk. Reviews also report that fasting reduces endurance performance and heightens reward from food cues. It is generally not recommended for people with eating disorders, pregnancy, children and adolescents, or those with diabetes who use glucose-lowering medicine.

chain: Whole days without calories lower weekly energy intake
Body weight and fat mass fall over weeks
angle.text: Fasting days reduce weekly calorie intake, which in studies lowers body weight and fat mass. People use this to look leaner in the face and midsection.

lead: Periodic whole-day fasting refers to water-only fasts lasting more than 24 hours, a category of intermittent fasting [1][2]. People use it to lower body fat and so improve how their face and body look, or as a tool to structure eating [3].

Randomised trials have studied 24-hour fasts on three non-consecutive days per week in women with overweight or obesity, comparing them with continuous calorie restriction [4][5]. Reviews describe weight loss from intermittent fasting as comparable to calorie-restricted diets, with loss coming from fat and some lean mass [2].
infobox: 5:2 diet, alternate-day fasting, extended water fasting
Fat loss, appetite and habit reset

paras: Intermittent fasting covers time-restricted eating, one-meal-a-day, alternate-day fasting, the 5:2 diet and periodic whole-day fasting, defined as water-only fasts longer than 24 hours [2]. Longer fasts of several days move the body from glucose use toward ketone production, with early weight loss that includes water and lean tissue [1].

Practitioners fast to cut weight without daily calorie counting, aiming for a lean face and visible muscle definition. Weight loss from intermittent fasting in human studies is generally 2.5 to 9.9 percent of body weight, comparable to calorie-restricted diets [2].

An eight-week randomised trial in 88 women with overweight compared intermittent fasting with 24-hour fasts three times weekly (at 100 or 70 percent of energy needs) with continuous restriction, measuring insulin sensitivity, body weight and composition [4]. A related trial examined clock-gene expression in muscle and fat after the same fasting pattern [5]. A randomised study found that a 24-hour fast heightened wanting and reward from food and food cues [3]. A review of fasting and endurance exercise reports reduced endurance performance in most human studies [6].

Short-term effects reported in reviews include hunger, irritability, dizziness, nausea and headaches. Prolonged fasts can lower sodium, potassium and magnesium, and refeeding after about four to five days without food can cause dangerous refeeding syndrome. Gallstone risk rises with rapid weight loss [1][2]. A review examined whether short-term fasting promotes pathological eating patterns [7].
